description: The persistent use of the '|||||' character sequence to separate discrete source articles within a single text entry.
explanation: Observed in 100% of the sampled records, this delimiter is the structural backbone of the 'document' field. It is a highly distinctive feature of the Multi-News dataset that allows a model to recognize transitions between independent journalistic perspectives on the same event, which is critical for high-fidelity synthesis of multi-source inputs.

description: The replacement of standard escape characters with the explicit string literal 'NEWLINE_CHAR' for structural formatting.
explanation: This feature has 100% prevalence across all samples. Distinct from generic text datasets that use standard '\n' characters, this specific encoding is a foundational 'DNA' marker. Synthetic data must replicate this exact string to maintain compatibility with the dataset's unique tokenization logic and structural schema.

description: Recurring parenthetical or bracketed strings that represent non-textual assets, such as '(PHOTO)', '[Infographic]', or 'IMAGE copyright REUTERS'.
explanation: Present in over 85% of samples, these artifacts are a domain-specific signature of web-scraped journalism. They indicate the presence of rich-media integrations and are essential for generating text that mimics the 'News/Journalism' domain's tendency to include captions and asset references within the body text.

description: Formal author credits and contact footers containing names, affiliations, and email addresses (e.g., 'By Justin Sink', 'jwarren@poynter.org').
explanation: This feature is a persistent norm in over 90% of samples. It distinguishes professional journalism from amateur blog content or generic prose. Synthetic generation requires these patterns to ensure that the generated 'document' field accurately reflects the institutional transparency and authorship standards inherent in the source DNA.

description: Recurring structural headers that link to related stories or internal articles, using keywords like 'RELATED:', 'ALSO:', and 'Read More:'.
explanation: Observed in roughly 80% of samples, this feature reflects the internal linking architecture of professional news sites. It is critical for synthesis because it dictates the 'inter-textual' flow of the dataset, where primary narrative text is punctuated by navigational content, which is a distinct characteristic of the news domain.
